title: Preprocessor Phases
concept: The preprocessor expands macros and directives before compilation to produce the actual code that gets compiled

steps.title: Preprocessor directive: #include
steps.explanation: **`#include <stdio.h>`** -- Code starting with `#` is a directive for the **preprocessor**. Preprocessing happens **before** compilation: it finds `stdio.h` in the system path and copies its **entire contents (thousands of lines)** into this location.

steps.title: Preprocessor directive: #define (macro constant)
steps.explanation: **`#define PI 3.14159`** -- Defines a **macro constant** called `PI`. The preprocessor performs a **simple text substitution**, replacing every occurrence of `PI` in the subsequent code with `3.14159`.

steps.title: Starting main function
steps.explanation: **`int main() {`** -- The program entry point where the compiler begins reading code after preprocessing is complete. At this point, the contents of `stdio.h` are already inserted, and all `PI` and `HELLO` tokens have been replaced with their actual values.

steps.title: Execution after macro substitution (string)
steps.explanation: **`printf("%s\n", HELLO);`** -- When the compiler sees this code, `HELLO` has already been replaced with `"Hello, World!"`, so it is 100% identical to `printf("%s\n", "Hello, World!");`.

steps.title: Variable declaration
steps.explanation: **`double r = 10.0;`** -- Creates the radius `r` in **stack memory** and initializes it to `10.0`. `double` is an 8-byte floating-point type that can represent approximately 15 decimal digits.

steps.title: Execution after macro substitution (number)
steps.explanation: **`double area = PI * r * r;`** -- To the compiler, this appears as `double area = 3.14159 * r * r;`. The result `3.14159 * 10.0 * 10.0` = `314.159` is stored in the new variable `area`.

steps.title: Printing the result
steps.explanation: **`printf("Area: %.2f\n", area);`** -- Prints the circle's area to **two decimal places**. In `%.2f`, `.2` means display only 2 digits after the decimal point. The third digit `9` is rounded up, outputting `314.16`.

steps.title: Program termination
steps.explanation:
**`return 0;`** -- An exit code telling the OS "completed successfully".

The key takeaway of this lesson is that **the preprocessor is a separate entity from the compiler**.

quiz.question: Can you get the memory address of a constant defined with #define MAX 100 using &MAX?
options: Yes. It is the same as a global variable.
No. It is replaced with the number before compilation, so it has no address.
It is possible with a specific option enabled.
The address exists in the stack area.
quiz.explanation: The macro constant `#define` is text replacement of source code during the preprocessor stage, so it does not exist as a variable at runtime.

misconceptions.wrong: #define is the same as defining a variable.
misconceptions.correct:
They are completely different.
A variable occupies memory space, but a macro is just text substitution in source code.
misconceptions.why: It does not perform type checking and unconditionally replaces text.

keyTakeaway: The preprocessor transforms the 'code text' itself before the compiler ever sees it.
